purpose: Sections 11/12: how repeated detections for the same claim aggregate, and how resolution works without ever deleting history.
dedupKey: (companyId, claimKey) - enforced by a real Postgres unique constraint (ClaimReviewItem @@unique), not merely application-level discipline.

dedupBehavior.newClaim: recordClaimReview() creates a new ClaimReviewItem row with status OPEN_REVIEW and one ClaimReviewObservation.
dedupBehavior.sameClaimSameOpenItem: A second detection for the SAME claimKey while the item is still OPEN_REVIEW appends a new ClaimReviewObservation (outcome OBSERVATION_APPENDED) - the item's top-level reasonCode/sourceEvidence/rationale fields are refreshed to the latest detection's evidence, but the full history of every prior detection survives in `observations`, never overwritten.
dedupBehavior.identicalRepeatedDetection: If the latest observation is byte-identical (same stage, reasonCode, detail) to the new one, no new observation row is written (outcome ALREADY_RECORDED) - an idempotent re-run of an unchanged pipeline over unchanged content does not grow the observation log without bound.
dedupBehavior.sameClaimResolvedItem: A detection for a claimKey whose item was previously RESOLVED_ACCEPTED/RESOLVED_REJECTED/SUPERSEDED automatically REOPENS it (status back to OPEN_REVIEW, a ClaimReviewDecision row with action=REOPEN is written) - a resolved claim never silently stays resolved while the pipeline is actively re-flagging it as still unresolved. This is the concrete implementation of Section 12's 'review items must not be permanent dead records' combined with this phase's own NO_SILENT_MATERIAL_FAILURE invariant.

crossStageAggregationExample: Section 11's own example (discovery -> compiler failure -> verification failure remaining ONE open item) is satisfied structurally: because this phase's single wired emission point sits downstream of semantic-coverage's own reconciliation (which already independently combines discovery+compiler+verifier evidence per claim before ever producing a SemanticUnitCoverageEntry), a claim that failed at multiple upstream stages naturally reconciles to ONE coverage entry, and therefore ONE ClaimReviewItem - the cross-stage aggregation problem is solved by REUSING Phase 3E's existing reconciliation rather than rebuilding it. A claim re-detected across separate coverage-audit RUNS (e.g. reruns of the pipeline over time as amendments/context evolve) is where recordClaimReview's own dedup-by-claimKey logic does the aggregating.

resolutionLifecycle.autoResolution: When a LATER coverage audit finds a previously-flagged claim now FULLY_REPRESENTED_VERIFIED, integrate.ts automatically resolves the item (action=ACCEPT, decidedBy=null, a note naming the algorithm version that resolved it) - Section 12's 'when semantic state is later successfully compiled/verified, the review item should transition appropriately,' implemented without waiting for a human when the pipeline's own evidence already resolves the gap.
resolutionLifecycle.humanResolution: resolveClaimReview() accepts an optional decidedBy (never fabricated - null unless a real reviewer identity is supplied, matching this codebase's established ExtractionCandidate.reviewedBy/LegalReviewRecord.reviewerName discipline) and a free-text note. Every transition writes a ClaimReviewDecision row; nothing is ever deleted or overwritten - the item's own top-level status/resolvedAt/resolvedBy/resolutionNote always reflect only the LATEST decision, matching CandidateReviewEvent's already-proven pattern.
resolutionLifecycle.neverDeleted: No function in service.ts ever deletes a ClaimReviewItem, ClaimReviewObservation, or ClaimReviewDecision row. The only deletion path is Postgres's own ON DELETE CASCADE from Company/Document deletion (matching every other per-company/per-document table in this schema) - never an application-level purge.
